correctness.rationale: With the diagonal intersection as origin, direct shoelace reduction gives \(CM=(pu+qv)/3\). The quadrilateral \(CCM\) is the intersection of the diagonal perpendicular bisectors, so its scalar products with \(u\) and \(v\) are \(p/2\) and \(q/2\). Equality is therefore exactly \(p=2q\cos\theta\) and \(q=2p\cos\theta\), whose complete solution is \(p=q=0\) or \(4\cos^2\theta=1\) with \(q=2p\cos\theta\). Convexity guarantees positive diagonal distances and nonzero area. The exact-arithmetic verifier independently checks the reductions and witness.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of when the quadrilateral generalized Euler line degenerates, for the exact center pair used in the foundational literature. It reveals a non-parallelogram \(60^\circ\) branch beyond the known equilateral sufficient class. The result is structural, parameter-complete in the quadrilateral case, and supplies explicit non-equilateral examples rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
